hints.title: Lexicographical Suffix Reversal
hints.text: Generating the next lexicographical permutation requires finding the smallest possible increase in value. From right to left, where does a decreasing sequence first break?

hints.title: Pivot Identification and Successor Swap
hints.text: Identify the first index i from the right where nums[i] is strictly less than nums[i + 1]. Then scan rightward to find the smallest number strictly greater than nums[i], swap them, and invert the remaining suffix.

hints.title: In-Place Two-Pointer Suffix Reversal
hints.text: After swapping the pivot with its successor, the suffix starting at i + 1 remains in descending order. Inverting this suffix with opposite-direction pointers restores ascending order in linear time.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of input array nums (1 <= N <= 100)
complexity.notes: Three linear passes at most: finding the pivot, finding the successor, and reversing the suffix in-place.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all N! permutations and sorting them requires factorial time and space, exceeding time limits.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant space in-place pointer swaps without allocating temporary array copies.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling entirely descending arrays (e.g., [3, 2, 1] -> [1, 2, 3]) and arrays with duplicate elements correctly.
